title: Why Do Birds Sing?
text:
Scientists study birds to learn how they communicate. Many male birds sing to attract females and to protect their territory. Each bird species has its own song, and young birds learn their songs by listening to adults. Some birds can even learn new songs during their lives.

In one study, researchers in a city noticed that birds sing at higher pitches than birds in the countryside. The noise from cars and buildings makes low sounds hard to hear. So the birds in the city sing higher to be heard. This shows that birds can change their songs when their environment changes.

questions.text: What do many male birds do with their songs?
options: Attract females and protect their territory

questions.text: Why do birds in the city sing at higher pitches?
options: Low sounds are hard to hear over city noise
They want to compete with other cities
Their songs are longer than usual
They are learning a new language

questions.text: What can be concluded about birds' songs?
options: Birds can change their songs when their surroundings change
All birds of one species sing the same song forever
Noise has no effect on how animals behave
Birds sing only early in the morning

questions.text: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Bird songs are shaped by communication and the environment
Birds are dangerous to people living in cities
Cities should plant more trees for birds
Birds travel long distances every winter

paragraph_translations: Cientistas estudam pássaros para entender como eles se comunicam. Muitos pássaros machos cantam para atrair fêmeas e para proteger seu território. Cada espécie de pássaro tem seu próprio canto, e os filhotes aprendem suas músicas ouvindo os adultos. Alguns pássaros podem até aprender novos cantos durante a vida.

Em um estudo, pesquisadores de uma cidade perceberam que os pássaros cantam em tons mais altos do que os pássaros do campo. O barulho de carros e prédios torna os sons graves difíceis de ouvir. Por isso, os pássaros da cidade cantam mais agudo para serem ouvidos. Isso mostra que os pássaros podem mudar seu canto quando o ambiente muda.
